requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

Each board visibly proposes an operator signature, identifiers for F1, F2 and F3, and a legible distinction between Regular and Express. Arrangement and styling are open; omission of any route or either service level fails.

The boards offer three distinguishable identity concepts through meaningful differences in signature, typography, route identification or visual language. Minor recoloring or rearrangement of the same concept does not establish three directions.

The strategy names one identifiable supplied direction. The identity sheet and presentation opening explicitly identify that same direction. Descriptive refinements are allowed, but an ambiguous selection, a different named choice or identification appearing only later in the presentation fails.

The strategy occupies one page and records its direction choice, one operator above three routes, one explicit primary color code, and how the two service levels differ. Explanatory wording may vary; missing decisions, multiple unresolved choices or additional pages fail.

The sheet supplies the selected signature, F1–F3 identifiers, both service labels, an identifiable typography specification and the exact primary color code recorded in the strategy. Layout is flexible; a missing component or a conflicting code fails.

The strategy and rules sheet agree on the one-operator, three-route architecture, primary color code and service distinction. The presentation explicitly repeats that hierarchy and code. Different explanatory phrasing is acceptable; contradictory architecture, changed codes or absent required statements fail.

Every application visibly uses the selected signature and primary color established by the strategy and rules sheet. Scale, placement and supporting route accents may adapt to the medium; omission, replacement of the signature or substitution of a different primary color fails.

Both artworks retain the reference hull outline, cabin proportions, window and door positions, right-facing orientation and full-body flat side view. Using the supplied carrier coordinate system, the signature lies within A at x=700–1900, y=785–870, and the assigned code and service label lie within B at x=1980–2380, y=770–860. Proportional scaling is allowed. The assignments are F1 Regular and F3 Express respectively; surrounding surfaces remain neutral and unbranded, with no template guides. Altered geometry, cropped framing, misplaced graphics or incorrect assignments fail.

The panel identifies P1 Harbor Hall and its F1 Cross Reach Regular and F2 Island Link Regular services. F1 lists P1 Harbor Hall then P2 Reed Bank, daily 07:00–21:00, every 20 minutes; F2 lists P1 Harbor Hall, P3 Lantern Isle and P4 North Quay, daily 08:00–20:00, every 40 minutes. A diagram labeled Schematic shows all four piers and all three routes, including F3 Quay Direct directly between P2 and P4. Geographic distortion and diagram orientation may vary; wrong connections, order, records or missing required information fail.

The static application identifies P1 Harbor Hall, carries both prescribed heading and status label, and shows the snapshot date 18 April 2028 and time 08:05. Exactly two departure rows appear: 08:20, F1 Cross Reach, Regular, to P2 Reed Bank; and 08:40, F2 Island Link, Regular, to P4 North Quay via P3 Lantern Isle. Layout may vary; abbreviated required names, extra departures, an invented F1 intermediate stop or mismatched fields fail.

The physical and mobile single tickets both contain the complete Single journey record: TW-1084, TIDEWAY FERRIES, Adult, F1 Cross Reach, Regular, from P1 Harbor Hall to P2 Reed Bank, 18 April 2028 and Scheduled departure 08:20. The Day pass contains TW-D2042, TIDEWAY FERRIES, Adult, Valid on 18 April 2028, All routes, F1, F2, F3 and Unlimited journeys on the valid date. All three show Sample. Field placement may differ across media; missing or changed values, reversed travel direction, disagreement between the TW-1084 versions, Express exclusion or entitlement beyond the valid date and operating windows fails.

Any network or service explanation remains compatible with bidirectional route operation, every listed stop being served by Regular, and direct P2–P4 operation without intermediate stops for F3 Express. Frequencies, when displayed, denote departure intervals rather than journey durations. A ticket or departure row may show its individual direction; it need not repeat the entire network explanation. Contradictory labels, arrows or service claims fail.

Review the entire video and its duration. It lasts 10 seconds, visibly connects the selected operator signature and F1–F3 identifiers with completed vessel, pier and ticket applications, and uses the chosen primary color. Editing and animation are open; replacement mockups that do not match the completed work, a missing named application category, a missing route identifier, conflicting branding or passenger-facing wording outside English fails.
requirementChecks.manualReason: Inspect complete SHA-bound original outputs. This source draft contains no completed professional or model-output review; partial-frame/page sampling cannot prove whole-output compliance.

requirementChecks.criteria: The presentation has at least eight pages and includes an identifiable storyboard for the service introduction, with a sequence connecting the selected identity, routes and completed applications. Page organization is flexible; fewer pages or a storyboard replaced by only a video title or link fails.

The presentation visibly incorporates all three initial boards, the strategy, identity rules, both vessel elevations, the pier panel, both ticket artworks and both mobile applications. Resizing and presentation framing are allowed when the source remains identifiable and its relevant content readable. Merely naming an earlier deliverable, substituting unrelated work or omitting any source fails.

Passenger-facing names, headings, instructions and explanatory copy are in English. Route codes, identifiers, numbers and color codes are acceptable. Passenger information conveyed only in another language fails.

Record 03-vessel-carrier.png as the identity image input defining the shared vessel object. It supplies carrier geometry rather than an existing operator logo or finished livery; this diagnostic does not score the outputs.

Record 04-vessel-application-zones.png as the constraint image input defining graphic placement limits. Its coordinate guides explain the application bounds and are not finished artwork; this diagnostic does not score the outputs.

Record 05-harbor-materials.png as the reference image input for waterfront atmosphere and material character, alongside the separately identified identity and constraint images. It is already named in the letter's Inputs section. Literal reproduction of its materials is not required, and this diagnostic never fails an output.
